✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: I just love Reverse puzzles, and this one hits my sweet spot. I spotted the pattern instantly, and it was really fun to solve. Also, I think the H part is a bit redundant since I managed to solve the puzzle by just getting the number of Carbon molecules. But if that preserves the nature of the puzzle, then I would keep it.
My Python input script: n = int(input()[1])

Test 1 (CH4) is the only case where the input formula doesn't follow the C[x]H[y] pattern. I suggest updating the cases as follows:

* CH4 (Test 1) => C2H6
* C2H6 (Validator 1) => C3H8
* C3H8 (Test 2) => C9H20

Thanks.
Thank you for pointing that out. I have modified the cases in a similar spirit, but have placed C9H20 such that each validator is 1 away from its respective test case.
That works too. My original intention was to minimise the changes, but your approach is absolutely fine. Thanks!
